NEW DELHI: The Sports Ministry has dropped under-fire para-shooting coach Jai Prakash Nautiyal from India's contingent for the Asian Para Games 2026, approving a 166-athlete squad for the continental event in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, amid a controversy-marred selection process that triggered protests by shooters and cyclists.The Games are scheduled to begin on October 18, with India set to compete across 10 disciplines. Long-serving national coach Jeevan L Rai has replaced Nautiyal in the squad following allegations of irregularities in the selection process.As per a PTI report, Nautiyal had faced allegations of not following established selection criteria and demanding kickbacks in exchange for selecting shooters. Several athletes protested outside the Sports Authority of India (SAI) headquarters, demanding his removal and an investigation into the charges.The aggrieved shooters also met Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya to present their grievances after attempting to disrupt the contingent's send-off ceremony last week.With 166 athletes approved, India will have a total contingent of 275, including 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff members.The 13-member shooting squad, which has been at the centre of the controversy, features Paralympic gold medallist Avani Lekhara and Mona Agarwal, among others.Agarwal recently secured a silver medal at the World Championships in Korea, earning India a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics.The Ministry has also resisted pressure for last-minute additions to the cycling squad despite protests by omitted athletes. Only Paralympian Arshad Shaik was approved from among those in contention, having comfortably met the selection criteria.Six other cyclists had been selected by the Cycling Federation of India and the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI), but were subsequently left out for failing to satisfy the prescribed criteria.The decision comes amid questions over the selection process, with athletes seeking greater transparency in the composition of the Indian contingent.Para-athletics forms the biggest part of India's contingent, with 62 athletes, including 46 men, and a support staff of 36. World Championships medallist Simran, a visually impaired sprinter, is also part of the squad. After her previous guide, Umar Saifi, was caught in a doping case, she will compete with a new guide, Shivam.India's other medal prospects include Paralympic silver medallist Bhavina Patel in table tennis and a strong badminton contingent of 28 players, comprising 17 men and 11 women.Former world No. 1 and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat and former Paralympic silver medallist Suhas Yathiraj headline the badminton squad, which has been allocated 11 support staff members.In archery, 19-year-old Sheetal Devi, a double gold medallist at the previous Para Asian Games, will be among India's leading contenders. The world champion will be joined by 18-year-old Payal Nag, who grabbed attention by defeating Sheetal at the World Archery Para Series in Bangkok earlier this year.With a sizeable contingent and several established champions in its ranks, India will look to make a strong impression in Japan, even as the selection controversy casts a shadow over the team's preparations.
Article Summary: The Sports Ministry has dropped under-fire para-shooting coach Jai Prakash Nautiyal from India's contingent for the Asian Para Games 2026. The decision comes amid questions over the selection process. India will have a total contingent of 275, including 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff members.

Article Title: Para-shooters allege corruption in Asian Games selection; PCI chief says process ‘100% fair’
Article Text:
Image credit: PCI

Shooters allege 20 per cent demand

Sandeep Kumar alleges selection bias

PCI rejects all allegations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ministry says grievances will be examined

The selection of India’s para-shooting team for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games has come under a cloud of controversy after a group of para-shooters alleged corruption and financial demands in the selection process.The shooters have sought an independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) and its Shooting Technical Committee (STC).In a representation submitted to the Director General of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Wednesday, the athletes alleged “illicit monetary extortion”, “brazen corruption” and violations of Sports Ministry guidelines.The Para Asian Games are scheduled to be held from October 18 to 24.One of the most serious allegations made in the representation was that athletes were being asked to give 20 per cent of their government cash awards as a condition for being selected for the national team.“Athletes are being coerced under severe duress into paying an illegal kickback of 20 per cent of their sanctioned government cash awards to designated committee office-bearers as a mandatory pre-condition for national team selection,” the representation alleged.The shooters also alleged that international quota places were not allocated purely on rankings and performances. They claimed financial considerations played a role in deciding who received the available places.According to their representation, two of the 15 international quota places available to India were surrendered because athletes next in line allegedly refused to meet the financial demands. The athletes also accused the selection committee of changing qualifying scores, ignoring Sports Ministry criteria and replacing an earlier selection panel without giving a recorded reason.P4 50m free pistol SH1 shooter Sandeep Kumar, ranked third in Asia, also questioned the selection decisions. He alleged that Rudrankksh Khandelwal, ranked 14th in Asia, was picked ahead of Akash, the Asian No. 1, and himself. Sandeep said he was “deeply aggrieved” by what he described as arbitrary decisions and violations of the selection rules.The shooters also questioned the appointment of an individual as a technical expert and Director of Operations, alleging that the person had no record of competing in an official shooting event.PCI president Devendra Jhajharia strongly rejected the charges and said the team had been selected strictly according to the prescribed rules.“The selection has been done as per the criteria. There has been no discrimination against anyone. The selections are 100 per cent fair and according to the Sports Ministry’s guidelines,” Jhajharia, a two-time Paralympics javelin gold-medallist, told PTI.Jhajharia also rejected Sandeep’s allegation that he was left out to make way for a shooter who had links with the coach.“Those are all false allegations,” Jhajharia said.A Sports Ministry source said genuine complaints raised by the para-shooters would be looked into. However, the source added that the Indian team for the Para Asian Games had already been finalised and could not be changed at this stage.The shooters have also indicated that they could take the matter to court if their allegations are not addressed.They said they may approach the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution, seeking a writ of mandamus and a court-monitored investigation into the selection process.
Article Summary: Shooters seek independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India. Two of the 15 international quota places available to India were surrendered because athletes next in line allegedly refused to meet the financial demands. The athletes also accused the selection committee of changing qualifying scores and ignoring Sports Ministry criteria.

Article Title: Asian Para Games send-off marred by protests over selection process
Article Text:
Indian para-shooters protest against PCI ahead of Asian Para Games 2026

New Delhi:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Payal’s coach omission adds another concern

The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games send-off ceremony was overshadowed by protests by para-shooters and para-cyclists here on Thursday, with athletes demanding fairness in selection for the multisport event, scheduled from Oct 18-24.As the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) held the ceremony at a city hotel in the presence of sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya , para shooters gathered outside the hotel lobby with placards and banners. Some protesters, including shooters Sandeep Kumar and Akash, had demonstrated at Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium on Wednesday.The protesters were initially dispersed by hotel security and later requested by Delhi Police personnel to leave as demonstrations were not permitted inside the premises. It is learnt that the minister wanted to meet them and discuss their concerns. He asked officials to check whether they were still around and waited in the lobby, but was informed that they had left.The minister then held discussions with ministry and Sports Authority of India (SAI) officials, with sources saying he stressed that the selection process should be fair and transparent.PCI president Devendra Jhajharia later defended the selections, saying PCI, ministry and SAI guidelines had been followed.He said athletes’ concerns had been heard and would be discussed with the ministry and PCI board, while leaving open the possibility of a review.Meanwhile, aggrieved para cyclists staged a protest outside Gate No. 1 of JLN stadium, demanding a fair selection. Arshad Shaikh, the lone cyclist selected for the contingent, joined his unselected teammates at the protest. A cyclists’ representative later met SAI officials at its headquarters in the evening and raised concerns over the exclusion of other recommended cyclists and its impact on India’s medal and Paralympic qualification prospects.The selection committee had recommended six cyclists, but only Shaikh made the contingent, prompting questions over the criteria used to reduce the list.Leading para archer Payal Nag’s coach Abhilasha Vedwan has been left out of the contingent, it’s been learnt. Payal has urged PCI to allow Abhilasha to travel, saying her medal prospects could suffer without her coach. Only Pankaj Singh and Gaurav Sharma have been approved as para archery coaches. Para badminton coach Gaurav Khanna has also been left out.
Article Summary: Athletes demand fairness in selection for the multisport event, scheduled from Oct 18-24. Paralympic Committee of India defends selections, leaving open possibility of review. Payal Nag’s coach Abhilasha Vedwan has been left out of contingent.

Article Title: ‘Carrying the tricolour is a different feeling’: Pramod Bhagat eyes gold at Para Asian Games
Article Text:
Pramod Bhagat

NEW DELHI: For a champion who has conquered the biggest stages in para badminton, the prospect of carrying the Indian flag as the flagbearer at the upcoming Para Asian Games for Pramod Bhagat is still an experience that stands apart from every medal and accolade.A gold medallist at the Tokyo Paralympics, Bhagat is preparing for his fifth Asian Para Games, carrying with him the experience of six medals, including two golds and four bronze. Yet, despite years of competing at the highest level, the responsibility of carrying the tricolour has brought a fresh sense of excitement.Bhagat recalled watching flag bearers lead the Indian contingent during his earlier appearances at the continental showpiece. The sight left a lasting impression on him, and now, as he prepares to take on that role himself, the feeling has become all the more meaningful.Having already won Paralympic gold, two Asian Games gold medals and the Padma Shri, Bhagat has experienced several defining moments in his sporting journey. However, he believes that the honour of being flag bearer cannot be compared with any of those achievements.“My expectation is gold, but it won't be easy,” he said, underlining the ambition that continues to drive him despite an already impressive medal collection.For Bhagat, longevity at the highest level has been built on the ability to adapt. Every edition of the Asian Para Games brings a different set of challenges, with opponents improving, preparations changing and the demands of the sport becoming more intense.“When you go to the second or third Asian Para Games, there is a difference of four years. A lot changes in four years. I try to learn from the past and move forward. I try to do my best, and I want to be successful,” he said.That approach has helped Bhagat remain a key figure in India's para badminton movement. His focus is not simply on defending his reputation but on finding ways to improve with every campaign. The target remains gold, but the process involves learning from previous performances, understanding the competition and making the most of his preparation.Beyond his personal ambitions, Bhagat is equally encouraged by the growing strength of Indian para badminton. With the sport attracting greater attention and Indian athletes making their presence felt internationally, expectations have risen.The goal, he said, is to push the country's medal count even higher.“We want to win more than 10 medals in the Para Asian Games,” Bhagat said, reflecting the confidence within the Indian contingent.The optimism is backed by a broader upward trend in India's para-sports performance. Bhagat pointed to the country's growing medal tally, noting that India had crossed the 100-medal mark at the previous Asian Para Games. For him, the progress is evidence of how sustained support, improved facilities and greater visibility can translate into results on the field.He believes the transformation has been particularly noticeable compared with the early days of his career, when govt assistance and public recognition for para badminton were more limited.Bhagat credited the government's growing involvement and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for taking a personal interest in para badminton, which he said had helped bring the sport greater recognition and publicity. That visibility, in turn, encouraged private organisations to come forward and support athletes.“When you get good support, and your equipment and training facilities improve, you perform well,” he said.The backing from both the government and the private sector, Bhagat believes, has helped create a stronger ecosystem for para athletes. Better equipment, improved training infrastructure and greater exposure have given players more opportunities to prepare and compete at the highest level. The rising medal count, he said, reflects the difference that such support can make.As India looks to build on its achievements at the continental level, Bhagat's campaign carries significance beyond the medals he hopes to win. He represents a generation of athletes who have benefited from a changing sporting environment while helping raise the profile of para badminton through their performances.For the veteran shuttler, though, the immediate task remains clear: prepare well, learn from experience and pursue gold. The flag-bearing honour has added another dimension to his campaign, giving him a responsibility that goes beyond his individual events.Bhagat knows that success will not come easily, but he is ready to embrace the challenge. And when he leads the Indian contingent with the tricolour in his hands, the moment will represent more than the achievements of a champion. It will reflect the journey of Indian para badminton, the progress of its athletes and the pride of representing the country.
Article Summary: Pramod Bhagat is preparing for his fifth Asian Para Games. He has won six medals, including two golds and four bronze. The gold medallist has already won Paralympic gold, two Asian Games gold medals and the Padma Shri.

Article Title: Para cyclists’ protest enters Day 2, even sole Asian Para Games pick joins stir
Article Text:
The cyclists continued their sit-in outside Jawaharlal Nehru stadium. (TOI Photo)

NEW DELHI: With the Asian Para Games fast approaching, India’s para cyclists are spending their days demanding answers instead of focusing on their preparations, as their protest against the team selection entered its second consecutive day on Friday.The cyclists continued their sit-in outside Gate No. 1 of Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium, braving the harsh sun and sitting on the pavement to demand justice and the inclusion of the athletes they say were overlooked despite meeting the selection criteria. Their grievance remains unchanged: six cyclists were recommended by the joint selection committee of the Cycling Federation of India (CFI) and Paralympic Committee of India (PCI), but only one — Arshad Shaikh — made the final contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.Even Shaikh, the lone cyclist selected, has joined the protest in solidarity with his fellow athletes. Instead of concentrating solely on his training and preparations for the continental event, he is standing alongside those questioning why they were left out.The athletes allege that their repeated appeals have failed to elicit a satisfactory response from the authorities. They want the selection decision reconsidered and a clear explanation of why the other recommended cyclists were excluded.The protesters say they will continue their agitation until their demands are met and the sidelined athletes are considered for selection.The dispute stems from the joint selection committee’s August 28 meeting, at which six cyclists were unanimously recommended for the Games. The list comprised Shaikh (MC2), Pavan Kumar Kommoji (MC3), Sameer (MC4), Prashant Arkal (MH4), Vishva Vasani (WC3) and Lisha Das (WC4).According to the athletes, their recommendations were based on performances, minimum qualifying standards, Asian and Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) rankings, and international qualification criteria. They have sought athlete-wise explanations and clarity on the basis on which the final list was reduced from six names to one.The cyclists have also pointed to the financial burden they have borne, claiming to have met expenses related to international participation, equipment and prosthetics themselves. With the Games looming, they argue that the uncertainty over their selection has added to the strain on athletes who should be preparing to represent the country.The Asian rankings cited by the athletes show that several of the excluded cyclists had competitive positions in their respective categories. In 2026, Shaikh was ranked second in road and third in track, while Kommoji was second and third, respectively. Sameer was eighth in road and fifth in track; Arkal was second in road; Vasani was third in road and second in track; and Das was sixth in road and second in track. Track rankings do not apply to the MH4 category.The athletes have also cited India’s position in the Asian UCI Nations Rankings as part of their argument over qualification slots, seeking transparency on how the available places were allocated.The cyclists’ protest comes amid wider discontent over selections for the Asian Para Games. Para-shooters have also continued to raise objections over the selection process. On Thursday, their protest at the Indian contingent’s send-off ceremony brought allegations of irregularities and favouritism into focus, with athletes questioning their exclusion from the squad. The allegations have been contested by officials, who have maintained that selection was based on the prescribed criteria.With both groups raising concerns over selection transparency, the protests have cast a shadow over India’s preparations for the Games. For the cyclists outside JLN stadium, however, the immediate demand remains simple: an explanation for the decision, a fair hearing and a resolution before the team departs for Japan.“We will continue our protest until our demands are met,” the cyclists have maintained.For athletes who should be sharpening their competitive edge ahead of a major international event, the question now is how long they will have to remain on the pavement before their pleas are heard.
Article Summary: The cyclists continued their sit-in outside Gate No. 1 of Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium. Six cyclists were recommended by the joint selection committee of the Cycling Federation of India (CFI) and Paralympic Committee of India. Only one — Arshad Shaikh — made the final contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.

Article Title: Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat, Bhavina Patel to lead India as flag bearers at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel

‘A very proud moment’

‘Fitting representatives of the Indian contingent’

NEW DELHI: After a successful Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya, where India finished fourth in the medal tally with 85 medals, including 21 gold, the country's para-athletes will look to carry the momentum into the Asian Para Games.Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel have been chosen as India's flag bearers for the Opening Ceremony of the Asian Para Games, scheduled to be held from October 18 to 24 in Nagoya, Japan.Bhagat, one of India's most decorated para badminton players, has won six Asian Para Games medals between 2014 and 2023, including two gold and four bronze. Patel, meanwhile, is among India's leading para table tennis players and has won two Asian Para Games medals — a silver and a bronze — between 2018 and 2023.Patel said being selected to carry the Tricolour was a matter of immense pride and hoped the honour would inspire the Indian contingent.“It is a very proud moment for me to be chosen as India's flag bearer,” Patel said in a release.“When you carry the Tricolour, you realise that you are representing something much bigger than yourself. I am excited to walk into the Opening Ceremony with Pramod and lead our contingent.I hope all our athletes compete with confidence, enjoy the moment and give their very best for India.”The Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) will formally send off the Indian contingent at a special ceremony on October 8. Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya will attend as chief guest, with Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse as the Guest of Honour.PCI president Devendra Jhajharia said Bhagat and Patel's achievements and resilience made them ideal choices to lead India at the continental para-sport showpiece.“It is a matter of immense pride for us to have Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel lead the Indian contingent at the Opening Ceremony,” Jhajharia said.“Both are exceptional champions who have contributed immensely to the growth of Indian para sport. Their journey, achievements and resilience make them fitting representatives of the Indian contingent, and I am confident they will inspire our athletes as they embark on this important campaign.”The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games will bring together para-athletes from across Asia, with India aiming to build on its growing success at major international competitions.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Coach row, court battles, clearance delays deepen chaos
Article Text:
File Pic: Shooter Manish Narwal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With less than a week to go before the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games starts, India’s preparations have been clouded by selection disputes, coaching omissions and administrative delays, leaving athletes in para shooting, cycling, badminton, table tennis and boccia grappling with uncertainty.On Monday, nine of India’s 13 selected para shooters met Sports Authority of India (SAI) officials and the sport’s project officer at SAI headquarters here, expressing dissatisfaction over the omission of chief coach J P Nautiyal from the contingent. Armourer and assistant coach Shivam Tyagi has also been left out.The aggrieved shooters urged authorities to reconsider the decision, with some expressing apprehension about competing without Nautiyal. Among those raising concerns were Manish Narwal, Mona Agarwal, Nihal Singh, Shrishti Arora, Swaroop Mahavir Unhalkar, Rakesh Nidagundi, Sumedha Pathak and Bhakti Sharma, who have won major international medals under his guidance.Bhakti, a deaf and non-speaking shooter who relies on specialised communication, reportedly broke down during the meeting, while Sumedha expressed doubts about competing without her coach.Pistol coach Rakesh Singh and support staff member Pavittar accompanied the shooters.The dispute comes as the ministry finally cleared the pending disciplines late on Monday evening, according to sources. The ministry’s push came as para badminton and table tennis contingents were scheduled to leave for Japan on Tuesday evening and there was considerable delay in announcing their final sanctions. With these approvals, the Indian contingent has been cleared across disciplines, barring pending court cases, including that of para cycling.The Oct 10 partial sanction covered eight disciplines and listed 128 athletes — 90 male and 38 female — alongside 91 officials, taking the contingent to 219 members. Badminton, table tennis and boccia were excluded at that stage.The delay also affected kit distribution. Athletes visiting the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) office on Monday afternoon to collect ceremonial and competition kits returned empty-handed as approvals were awaited. Pramod Bhagat, India’s opening-ceremony flag-bearer, had worn fellow shuttler Sukant Kadam’s ceremonial outfit at the October 8 send-off because his own did not fit.Last-minute clearances have left athletes with little time to correct ill-fitting kits, organise equipment, and prepare for departure. In table tennis, competition begins on Oct 16, following classification checks on Oct 15. Wheelchair players need time to acclimatise and adjust their equipment, while paddlers will have just a day to rest after reaching Nagoya before classification begins.Despite the final approvals, five badminton names — Chirag Baretha, Manisha Patel, Shashank Kumar, Ammu Beulah Mohan and Rachna Patel — have not been sanctioned, sources said. LY Suhas has been cleared. Kalpesh Thakkar, secretary of the Table Tennis Association of Baroda, has also not been cleared.In para cycling, five qualified athletes have challenged their exclusion in the Delhi High Court under Articles 14 and 21, questioning the decision to retain only one cyclist despite six recommendations. The case will be heard again on Tuesday, with an interim decision expected.
Article Summary: Nine of India’s 13 selected para shooters met Sports Authority of India (SAI) officials. They expressed dissatisfaction over the omission of chief coach J P Nautiyal. The aggrieved shooters urged authorities to reconsider the decision. The dispute comes as the ministry finally cleared the pending disciplines late on Monday.

Article Title: UCL Round-up: PSG sink Manchester City, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid stage late comeback on record-breaking night

PSG stun Manchester City, Real Madrid stage comeback

Liverpool, Betis and other results

The UEFA Champions League witnessed a record-breaking night of goals on Wednesday, as Paris Saint-Germain defeated Manchester City 4-2 and Real Madrid scored three late goals to beat Roma 4-3.A total of 78 goals were scored across Matchday 2, surpassing the previous record of 71 goals set during Matchday 3 last season. Vitinha added the third in the 32nd minute, leaving City struggling to respond.Erling Haaland pulled one back in the 53rd minute, but Maghnes Akliouche restored PSG’s three-goal advantage. Haaland scored again in the 75th minute, bringing City back into the contest, but PSG held on for the win. The match was Manchester City’s first European fixture since being charged with financial rule breaches in the Premier League.Real Madrid produced a dramatic finish against Roma. After the home side took a 3-1 lead, Madrid substitutes Carlos Espí and Endrick scored late goals to level the match.Antonio Rüdiger then netted the winner from close range following a corner, securing a 4-3 victory. Kylian Mbappé also scored on his 100th Champions League appearance, becoming the youngest player to reach that milestone at 27.Liverpool defeated LASK 6-3, with Bradley Barcola scoring a hat trick. Ronald Araújo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also found the net for Liverpool, while LASK scored three times in response.Real Betis beat Porto 3-2 in a heated contest, with Isco scoring the decisive penalty late in the game. Abde Ezzalzouli also scored a spectacular goal for Betis.Elsewhere, Aston Villa thrashed Fenerbahçe 6-0, Bodø/Glimt beat Borussia Dortmund 1-0, and Stuttgart defeated Slovan Bratislava 3-0. Shakhtar Donetsk overcame AEK Athens 3-1 in London, while Feyenoord came from behind to defeat Como 3-2.
Article Summary: A total of 78 goals were scored across Matchday 2, surpassing the previous record of 71 goals set during Matchday 3 last season. Barcelona's Joao Cancelo, right, celebrates with teammates after scoring his side's first goal during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Galatasaray and Barcelona in Istanbul, Turkey, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Khalil Hamra)

Barcelona and Arsenal secured convincing wins in the Champions League on Tuesday, while Bayern Munich suffered a late setback against Viking in Norway.Meanwhile, Manchester United’s poor form continued with a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, increasing pressure on coach Michael Carrick.Barcelona came from behind to beat Galatasaray 4-1 in Istanbul, extending its winning streak to 10 games in all competitions.Arsenal also impressed with a 3-0 victory over Lille, while Inter Milan suffered a surprising 4-3 home defeat to Club Brugge.Barcelona faced an early challenge when Aleksey Batrakov put Galatasaray ahead. Article Title: Lisandro Martinez blasts Manchester United hierarchy in fiery rant; Wayne Rooney brands comments ‘disrespectful’ after UCL loss to Atletico Madrid
Article Text:
Lisandro Martinez and Wayne Rooney

Wayne Rooney questions Martinez’s motives

Rooney draws on his own experience

Ashley Young backs Rooney’s assessment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has sparked controversy after openly criticising the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, with former United captain Wayne Rooney accusing the Argentine of being disrespectful to his teammates.The defender’s post-match interview raised questions about United’s summer recruitment strategy and the club’s readiness to compete at the highest level. Martinez expressed frustration with the lack of further investment in the squad, suggesting that the club’s decision-makers should have done more after the team secured its return to the Champions League.Speaking to Amazon Prime, Martinez said: “I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it’s a reflection in the mirror of how is our club at the moment,” Martinez told Amazon Prime. “We did a fantastic season last season. And now we expect more from the top, from up, to bring more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well, and today also Atletico they have an amazing team and they deserved to win today.“I expect more from our technical director. I would have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it’s just important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”United, under director of football Jason Wilcox, reportedly invested around $213 million during the summer transfer window, bringing in players including Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite that spending, the club has endured a disappointing start to the campaign.The defeat in Madrid extended United’s winless streak across all competitions to five matches. The team has managed just one Premier League victory and currently sits 13th in the standings.Martinez also reflected on the contrast between last season’s progress and the team’s current struggles, expressing disappointment with the performance in Spain.“Last season we did everything; we created the base to be an amazing team,” Martinez said. “It's annoying, disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here, it's disappointing.”Atletico made an immediate impact, with Pablo Barrios scoring in the opening minute before Ademola Lookman added a second-half goal to secure the victory. The result has increased scrutiny on United head coach Michael Carrick as the club attempts to recover from its difficult start.However, Martinez suggested that the focus on managerial changes overlooks other issues within the organisation.“You start changing, changing, changing manager. But what about other areas?” Martinez said. “I can’t say more.”Rooney strongly disagreed with Martinez’s decision to air his frustrations publicly, arguing that concerns about recruitment and squad quality should be discussed internally rather than through the media.Speaking on Amazon Prime after the match, the former United striker said: "I actually disagree as I thought it was a good performance."It's a difficult one because I always used to feel like I was outspoken as a player, and you want to have your opinion, but I think he's maybe gone too far; that should be down to the manager, and that should stay internal because the fans want to hear the players speak and they want to see them care."He clearly cares and wants the club to invest more money and more players, and if they do that, I think he'll be one of the players out the door if I'm being honest with his performances."His performances haven't been good enough but I think in some ways he is right, in terms of the club need to invest more at the top end of the pitch and in defence as well."I think it looks like that was a bit of an agenda from him because that doesn't mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better."Although Rooney acknowledged that United need improvements in key areas, he questioned why Martinez chose that particular moment to make his concerns public."I think Martinez was very premeditated. Why is he doing the interview after this game? Has he put himself forward, I very rarely hear him speak."It looked a bit premeditated and something he spoke about with his team to get out there. It's sad because when you need everyone to stick together as players, you can't be told what's going on above you."So you need them players, the manager, the coaching staff to stick together when you're having a difficult time; otherwise, something like that will rip a dressing room apart."I think it's a bit disrespectful to his team-mates as well because he's disrespecting his team-mates, he's saying they're not good enough. So he's saying his team-mates aren't good enough, so it's disrespectful."Rooney also suggested that captain Bruno Fernandes would be better placed to raise concerns on behalf of the squad, while insisting that any issues should be addressed privately."I think Bruno is probably the only one who has any right coming out and saying something like that if I'm being honest as captain. And even then, it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen."Players have conversations with the manager, the manager then has a conversation with the board, but that interview there, it's not going to help the situation the club is in at the minute."Now all that's going to bring is more noise around it, the players are unhappy, they're unsettled, they don't trust in their own team-mates, that's not going to help at all."Rooney went further when discussing whether Martinez was attempting to reflect the frustrations of Manchester United supporters. While expressing appreciation for the defender’s ability, he pointed to his injury record and questioned whether he had done enough to speak on behalf of the squad."I don't think he's really connected with the fans since he's been here, to be honest, because he's been injured a lot."I actually like him, I think he's a good player, but he's been injured, so for the money the Man United pay for him, he hasn't given the service back really."From that point of view, that's not me being disrespectful, I just think he's had a lot of injuries and hasn't played that much."So I think he's trying to speak on behalf of the players if you like, but I think he's done it in the wrong way, as I said before, I think that should be from the captain if that's the case."For me, it's disrespectful to his teammates. I had a similar situation when I went in and asked Alex Ferguson about what players we were bringing in, and I apologised two days later."So I can speak from experience of what he's just done, I think it is very disrespectful, there's a lot of young players in that dressing room as well that need some guidance from experienced players."Drawing on his own playing career, Rooney argued that experienced footballers have a responsibility to guide younger teammates, particularly during difficult periods. He also indicated that the club’s board may need to respond to Martinez’s remarks."The board have to look at that, and they probably have to take some action on that, because that's just disrespecting the whole football club."Yes, there's issues, everyone wants more players and better players, but this is the players you've got. As a player, you've got to get on with it."You've got to go and show why you're a World Cup winner, as I said before. So, I think the board have to either come out and speak on it, or maybe he's done that to flush them out and get them to speak to the fans, but I just think it's the wrong time, and it's not going to help anyone."Former Manchester United player Ashley Young also questioned Martinez’s timing, agreeing that the club’s recruitment process needs improvement but stressing that players must take responsibility for their performances.Young acknowledged that United could have strengthened other areas of the squad during the summer, particularly in attack and defence. However, he argued that rebuilding the team cannot happen all at once."Of course, there is a lot of it that the players are talking about it. We spoke before the game about how the club needed to invest more, but when they've invested in the midfield but what does he want?"Go and buy a whole new team? They're not going to do that. They need to start in different positions. They could've bought up front or in defence but they didn't. He's just come off the pitch, emotions are running high, we know that."But we know the recruitment has to work, it has to be better but they've got to take time and do it. The players have got to take it upon themselves, 'we're the players that are in this team, we're the players that are in this squad and go out on the pitch.'"They are the ones who have to go and produce and show what they're about. There's not going to be any change now until January."With the January transfer window still some way off, United face mounting pressure to improve results with their existing squad.Martinez’s criticism has highlighted concerns about recruitment and the club’s direction, but Rooney and Young believe that publicly airing such frustrations risks creating further divisions inside the dressing room at a time when unity is crucial.
Article Summary: Lisandro Martinez criticises Manchester United hierarchy after 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid. Former United captain Wayne Rooney accuses Martinez of being disrespectful to his team-mates. United have endured a disappointing start to the season, with just one Premier League win.

Barcelona return to Kolkata after eight years

Kolkata is preparing for another taste of El Clasico, with Barcelona and Real Madrid legends set to bring their famous rivalry to India on November 25. The exhibition will give fans another chance to see former stars of the Spanish giants together on Indian soil, following Real Madrid Legends’ victory in Mumbai last year. With Luis Figo, Carles Puyol and Iker Casillas among the names reportedly expected, the contest could be a significant occasion for a city with a long relationship with world football.West Bengal sports minister Indranil Khan announced on Tuesday that Barcelona Legends and Real Madrid Legends will meet at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, popularly known as the Salt Lake Stadium, on November 25.The official squads have not yet been confirmed, although Portuguese great Figo, who represented both Spanish rivals during his playing career, and former Barcelona captain Puyol are among the prominent names expected to feature, alongside Spain’s World Cup-winning goalkeeper Casillas.This will be the second time the two clubs’ legends have faced each other in India, following their meeting at Mumbai’s DY Patil Stadium last year. Real Madrid Legends won that contest 2-0, with former striker Fernando Morientes and David Barral scoring the goals.The two sides also met in Miami earlier in 2026, playing out a 1-1 draw in which Martin Montoya scored for Barcelona and Álvaro Negredo found the net for Real Madrid.Their Kolkata encounter will now bring the exhibition rivalry to another Indian city, with the final line-ups still to be confirmed.For supporters, the appeal lies in seeing familiar names from two of football’s most celebrated clubs share the same pitch again. Figo’s unusual connection to both sides adds another layer of interest, while the prospect of Puyol and Casillas appearing gives fans further reason to watch for the official team announcements.Barcelona’s visit will mark their first appearance in Kolkata since September 2018, when they faced Indian football giants Mohun Bagan at the same stadium. The Catalans won that match 6-0, with Javier Saviola, Roger Garcia, Pedro Landi, Jari Litmanen and Jofre Mateu among the scorers.Kolkata has hosted some of football’s biggest names over several decades, earning a reputation as one of India’s most devoted footballing cities. One of its most memorable occasions came in 1977, when Brazilian legend Pelé led New York Cosmos against Mohun Bagan at Eden Gardens, while German giants Bayern Munich visited the city in 2008 to play the Kolkata club in a friendly.The city also hosted Lionel Messi’s only appearance on Indian soil in 2011, when Argentina faced Venezuela at the Salt Lake Stadium. More recently, the venue staged high-profile international friendlies in early October 2026, as India faced five-time world champions Brazil and two-time World Cup winners Uruguay.The November exhibition will add another prominent fixture to that history, bringing together two clubs whose rivalry has captivated football supporters across generations. Although the squads remain unconfirmed, Kolkata’s latest football occasion already has a clear attraction: another chapter of El Clasico, this time featuring the legends who helped make it famous.
Article Summary: Barcelona Legends and Real Madrid Legends will meet at Kolkata's Salt Lake Stadium on November 25. Luis Figo, Carles Puyol and Iker Casillas are among the prominent names expected to feature. It will be the second time the two clubs’ legends have faced each other in India, following their meeting at Mumbai’s DY Patil Stadium last year. The official squads have not yet been confirmed.

Article Title: Messi reportedly set to present Ballon d’Or to winner despite being a nominee himself, fans call out awkward Yamal scenario
Article Text:
Lionel Messi has reportedly been lined up to present the 2026 Ballon d’Or, despite being among the 30 nominees himself.

How the Messi Ballon d’Or presenting rumour started

Messi remains a contender for his ninth Ballon d’Or

Oct 10, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Inter Miami CF forward Leo Messi (10) celebrates after scoring against the D.C. United during the second half at Nu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY

Lamine Yamal theories and memes have already taken off

20-year-old soccer star Lionel Messi helps to bathe Lamine Yamal, who was merely six months old at the time, during a photo session in Sept. 2007 in the dressing room of the Camp Nou stadium in Barcelona, Spain. (AP Photo/Joan Monfort)

Lionel Messi could reportedly present the trophy at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, even as he remains a nominee for the award himself. The same report suggests his family could join him at the event. While neither detail has been confirmed, the possibility of the eight-time winner taking on a presenter’s role while still in contention for a ninth Ballon d’Or makes for an interesting scenario.The speculation originated with a Spanish independent football reporter Juan Jesus, who claimed on X that Messi would attend the ceremony on October 26 and personally hand the trophy to this year’s winner. The claim subsequently spread across football aggregation accounts, fan pages and online sports coverage, turning an unverified report into a talking point ahead of the ceremony.Separate reports have also suggested that Messi will attend the ceremony with his family. Their attendance would certainly make sense if the Argentine decides to attend, particularly with the possibility of celebrating a record-extending ninth Ballon d’Or alongside his family, but neither Messi nor the organisers have confirmed those plans.The ceremony will take place at the London Palladium on October 26, marking the 70th edition of football’s most prestigious individual award.For the first time, the event will be held in London, with organisers honouring Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the inaugural Ballon d’Or in 1956.Neither France Football nor UEFA has officially confirmed Messi’s reported presenting role, and his attendance remains unverified.Messi’s reported role as a presenter is particularly intriguing because he is also among the 30 nominees for this year’s award. The 39-year-old Inter Miami forward returns to the shortlist after missing out in the previous two editions and remains in contention for an unprecedented ninth Ballon d’Or.Messi’s 2026 campaign gives him a substantial case to make, having helped Argentina reach the World Cup final with eight goals and four assists across eight matches. He has also continued delivering for Inter Miami, recording 23 goals and 11 assists during the 2026 MLS regular season.The Argentine last won the Ballon d’Or in 2023, following his decisive contribution to Argentina’s 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar. Another victory would extend his record as the award’s most successful recipient, potentially creating an awkward scheduling problem if he had also been invited to present the trophy.A ceremony cannot realistically have Messi hand himself the award, should he win, so organisers would need another presenter for that moment. The claim that he has been selected to present the trophy does not establish that he has lost the race, particularly while his candidacy remains active and the result has not been announced.Much of the online reaction has centred on Lamine Yamal, with some fans imagining Messi handing the teenager his first Ballon d’Or as a symbolic passing of the torch. Their connection stretches back to a famous 2007 UNICEF calendar photograph showing a 20-year-old Messi bathing five-month-old Yamal, making the prospect of the Argentine presenting him with football’s biggest individual prize feel almost scripted.Some supporters have consequently joked that the rumour has already given away the winner, suggesting that the organisers have created an obvious publicity moment around the pair’s remarkable connection.Fans have also turned the rumour into a meme, comparing Messi presenting the award to Barack Obama handing himself a medal.The family angle, at least, seems entirely plausible. With Messi having retired from international football, the Ballon d’Or could be another occasion for his loved ones to watch him take centre stage, especially if he ends up adding a ninth title to his collection.For now, Messi remains a nominee, the reported presenting role remains unconfirmed and the winner will only become clear at the ceremony. Until then, fans can enjoy imagining the possibilities, even if the most entertaining scenario would require the organisers to find someone else to hand Messi his ninth Ballon d’Or.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi could present the trophy at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, even as he remains a nominee for the award himself. The same report suggests his family could join him at the event. The ceremony will take place at the London Palladium on October 26, marking the 70th edition of football’s most prestigious individual award.

Article Title: OFFSIDE: Why Ronaldo vs Messi is now less a debate and more a tragicomedy
Article Text:
Why Ronaldo vs Messi is less debate and more tragicomedy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hello and welcome to another edition of Offside.The most sublime TV shows often spiral into mediocrity. Game of Thrones was very hard to care about after Season 5, when they ran out of George RR Martin’s books and had to come up with something on their own, which was AI slop even before generative AI had hit our lives. House MD went downhill the moment they started focussing more on the Doc’s drug issues than the actual medicine. The same goes for Mad Men, where Don Draper’s personal issues became an albatross around a great show’s neck. And the same happened with The Boys, which began as an apt satire of our superhero-obsessed culture before becoming so bad in subsequent seasons that only Homelander’s narcissism – which started to resemble that of another man with blonde/orange hair who thinks he’s omnipotent – and Billy Butcher’s cussing kept the show from becoming completely banal. By the last season, it was running on fumes, and there was only one scene that made it worth watching all of them: Homelander losing his powers and getting tea-bagged by Butcher.It was worth the wait to see the world’s most powerful creature with a God complex being reduced to a mere mortal, more so since he had just killed Frenchie. And oddly, that final battle is starting to resemble the late-stage international careers of Lionel Messi and Ronaldo.And to put a cherry on the comparison, late-stage Ronaldo is starting to look even more like Homelander.Jeffrey Archer – a novelist known as much for his lifelong mendacity as his ability to pen compelling stories – had a format he first introduced with Kane and Abel and perfected over the years. In this format, he would take two contrasting Archer-types (pun intended) and run the rule over their entire lives from birth to death.Now, if he were to write about Messi and Ronaldo, he would probably begin with their lives. One, a tiny kid born in a middle-class neighbourhood in Rosario to the manager of a steel manufacturing unit and his wife, who worked in a magnet manufacturing plant.The other, a boy born into considerably more modest circumstances on the Portuguese island of Madeira, whose father worked as a municipal gardener and kit man at a local football club and named him not after the Brazilian footballer of the same name but after Ronald Reagan.Both would leave their homes soon.Messi, whose growth hormone deficiency threatened to derail any career in sports, finally signed a contract with Barcelona – famously drafted on tissue paper – while Ronaldo joined Sporting’s academy in Lisbon, eventually attracting the attention of a Scotsman who knew a thing or two about forging youngsters into world-beaters.After torturing United’s stalwarts in a friendly – this was a time when they were Premier League beaters and not a banter club – the aforementioned Scotsman refused to leave the Sporting ground till they signed him. Ronaldo spent six years in Manchester, where his insouciant petulance was kicked out of him – sometimes literally – by Messrs Keane, Scholes and other members of the United first team, resulting in three Premier League titles, the Champions League and his first Ballon d’Or.Meanwhile, Messi progressed through La Masia to Barcelona’s first team, learning at the feet of Ronaldinho before Pep Guardiola pulled off football’s greatest switcheroo by moving him to a false nine role. He slowly became the footballer who looked like he had a button that allowed him to go into bullet-time mode.Messi’s and Ronaldo’s destinies – like football’s Karna and Arjuna – were always intertwined, and the Argentine got the first laugh when Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona beat Manchester United 2-0 in a match where the Blaugrana made the Red Devils look like a Sunday league team. The cherry on top for Messi fans was the fact that at a time when Ronaldo was revered for his aerial prowess, it was the 5’7” magician who scored a header.Ronaldo would eventually move to Madrid in 2009 for a then-world-record £80 million, bringing the two men into direct conflict in what would become football's greatest individual rivalry, consuming everything like a supernova. Between them, they broke every scoring record, shared every Ballon d’Or, and the only meaningful interruption to their rivalry came when someone had to collect the trophy from the podium and hand it to one of them.But all great stories have to end, with Ronaldo moving to Juventus, returning to United and then leaving for Saudi Arabia after an almighty fit.Messi, meanwhile left a debt-riddled Barcelona, went to PSG, where even the Neymar-Messi-Mbappé troika failed to recreate the magic before settling in Miami in Mammon’s, sorry, David Beckham’s warm embrace.Their international careers, however, had different trajectories, with Messi failing to replicate his club form for his country, a Maradona-esque burden that seemed to hang heavy over him, with every failure treated as evidence that he wasn’t as great as his coke-loving predecessor. He even announced his retirement in 2016 before eventually winning the Copa América in 2021 and leading Argentina to the World Cup in Qatar in 2022.The 2026 World Cup ended in heartbreak, but Messi was never a burden for his team, and it appeared that the rest of the Argentina team would run through a brick wall for him, and perhaps if they had bothered to play a little football too, the final result could have been different. Messi signed off with one final match after his father and manager passed away.Ronaldo, on the other hand, won Euro 2016 with Portugal, though during the final he was off the pitch with an injury, and two UEFA Nations League titles. During the World Cup, it actively felt like Ronaldo was becoming a burden on his Portuguese teammates. Throughout his career, Ronaldo’s sphere of influence had decreased, first from the entire pitch to a small area in the penalty box, and even that skillset appeared to desert him in his final days in a Karna-like way.And yet Ronaldo appeared to persist with his national team, showing the sort of insouciance that was associated with a pre-Ferguson Ronaldo. He eventually left the Portugal camp.And then, in an extraordinarily long Instagram post of nearly 2,000 words that could masquerade as an Offside column, Ronaldo wrote the sort of explainer that SEO guys dream about and released it hours before Messi’s final farewell.The 11-slide Instagram manifesto began with a revelation that Ronaldo had prepared his retirement letter after the 2026 World Cup, but the 41-year-old claimed he was persuaded to stay and that the board had consulted him before appointing Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo also invoked Simão Coutinho, Al-Nassr’s sporting director, pointing out that Jesus, in a previous avatar, had reported to Coutinho. That felt oddly like the Portuguese version of the Delhi saying: “Tu jaanta hai mera baap kaun hai?”In every single way, it was reminiscent of late-stage Homelander becoming more and more convinced of his own immortality and becoming increasingly unhinged before meeting his fate at Billy Butcher’s hands.There was a time when the Messi vs Ronaldo GOAT debate had an inkling of merit.At that time, when Ronaldo said he was the “best in the world”, the world might have disagreed with him, but the way he went toe-to-toe with Messi suggested there was some meat to the debate. But in recent years, it feels more like a hollow chant, one that doesn’t convince anyone except Piers Morgan or iShowSpeed.Many years ago, Sir Alex Ferguson’s firm hand had forged Ronaldo’s career, turning a gifted teenager into a world-beater. In the late stages of his career, it’s quite clear there’s no Ferguson-like figure to lend him a shoulder, or perhaps Ronaldo has become a person who no longer listens to anyone else. Either way, it’s sad for anyone who has followed his career with interest to see what has become of the teenager of touch and tease who first made his Manchester United debut against Bolton and blew everyone away with his skills.And if Jeffrey Archer were to write the final chapter of these two intertwined lives, he would probably relish the irony that the boy from Rosario, who needed help to grow, eventually learnt when to say goodbye, while the boy from Madeira, whom Ferguson taught to grow up, appears unable to do the same. Homelander had to lose his powers before realising that he was a mere mortal. Ronaldo, thankfully, still has time to write a different ending but it's unlikely will. After all, the greatest tragedy would be for a man who spent his entire career defying the limits of human ability to be remembered for his inability to accept them.
Article Summary: The most sublime TV shows often spiral into mediocrity. Game of Thrones was very hard to care about after Season 5, when they ran out of George RR Martin’s books and had to come up with something on their own. And the same happened with The Boys, which began as an apt satire of our superhero-obsessed culture before becoming so bad in subsequent seasons. And oddly, that final battle is starting to resemble the late-stage careers of Lionel Messi and Ronaldo.

Article Title: "Curse has been lifted": NFL podcaster Will Compton reveals wife is expecting their first son after 2 daughters in growing family
Article Text:
Will Compton and his wife, Charo, are expecting their first son after welcoming two daughters (Laura Moll/Via PEOPLE)​

Will Compton announces first son after two daughters

Will Compton and his wife, Charo, have shared news that gives their family another reason to celebrate. The Bussin’ with the Boys podcaster, 37, announced that the couple are expecting their third child, a boy, after raising two daughters, Cerulean Belle, 4, and Scottie, 22 months. Compton marked the announcement with a football reference, declaring that the “curse” had been lifted. But the pregnancy announcement carried a deeper meaning for the couple. Charo also opened up about a miscarriage last year and the IVF journey that led to their latest pregnancy, describing their son as both a miracle and a rainbow baby.The couple announced the pregnancy in a joint Instagram post on Tuesday, October 13. Charo shared their excitement about welcoming a boy next spring, writing, “Our miracle + our rainbow, all in one… baby BOY Compton making his appearance next spring 🩵,” before adding, “we are so indescribably grateful and joyful for such a precious gift 🕊️ also: a party of 5?!”For Compton, the news also offered a chance to joke about the arrival of a son after two daughters. In his own Instagram post, he shared a picture with Scottie while holding several sonograms.“An A-Gap Successor is on the way,” he wrote. “The curse has been lifted 🔵🔵🔵.”The former NFL linebacker also included AI-generated images imagining his future child in a football jersey and taking selfies at the gym. The playful posts fit the football-focused humor familiar to listeners of his podcast, but Charo's announcement offered a more personal account of what the couple had experienced before reaching this point.Charo opens up about miscarriage and IVF journeyCharo revealed that she suffered a miscarriage just over a year ago, describing the pregnancy as a spontaneous and unexpected surprise. Her post came during October, which is Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month.“October is pregnancy + infant loss awareness month, and it was just over one year ago that I suffered a miscarriage of a spontaneously-conceived wonderful, happy surprise,” she wrote.She said the loss brought intense sadness. The couple eventually decided to undergo another IVF cycle, which resulted in the current pregnancy.“The journey is never linear and I feel profoundly for all versions of this story; especially the ones in the messy middle, without a ‘happy ending’ yet,” Charo continued. “Though it may often feel like it, you are never alone.”The announcement also drew a joking reference to ESPN college football analyst Kirk Herbstreit. One commenter suggested Compton had taken notes from Herbstreit, who discussed a supposed method for conceiving boys during an August appearance on Bussin’ with the Boys.Herbstreit said his wife, Alison, would perform a handstand after sex because she had heard male sperm were faster. The couple have four sons: twins Jake and Tye, Zak, and Chase. Co-host Taylor Lewan also said he and his wife tried the same approach, though they have three daughters.There is no scientific evidence that handstands after sex can determine a baby's sex. For the Comptons, the news of their son comes after a much more difficult journey, making the excitement behind their announcement especially personal.
Article Summary: Will Compton and his wife, Charo, are expecting their first son after welcoming two daughters. The couple announced the pregnancy in a joint Instagram post on Tuesday, October 13. Charo also opened up about a miscarriage last year and the IVF journey that led to their latest pregnancy.

Article Title: Terry Bradshaw and Tammy’s ER meeting led to romance, but one first-date detail made her hesitate to call him back
Article Text:
Terry Bradshaw and Tammy Bradshaw first met in 2003 (Instagram)

Terry Bradshaw’s hospital encounter with Tammy led to an unexpected first date

Tammy’s hesitation came as Terry Bradshaw faced doubts about marriage

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Terry Bradshaw was not looking for a new relationship when he met Tammy in a Texas hospital in 2003. The former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback had been through three divorces and was trying to focus on his mental health. Then an injured horse trainer brought him to Baylor Scott & White Medical Center in Grapevine, where Tammy was working in radiology. Their first meeting sparked an immediate attraction, but dating a famous NFL figure was another matter. Even after a successful first date, Tammy questioned whether she was ready for the life that came with him.Bradshaw, now 78, accompanied a horse trainer from his ranch to the hospital for an X-ray after the trainer broke an ankle. That was where he first saw Tammy, then a radiology manager and educator.“They had to X-ray [the trainer’s broken ankle],” he recounts to PEOPLE from the kitchen table at the couple’s horse breeding ranch in Saint Jo, Texas, last month. “And through the doors comes blondie. I went, ‘Oh my God, is she ever more gorgeous?’ I automatically said, ‘Oh, wow.’ “Bradshaw tried to strike up a conversation while Tammy focused on her work.She remembers the exchange with humor, saying, “I’m just trying to do my job.”Still, the attraction was not one-sided. Tammy recalls making eye contact with the former quarterback and being struck by his eyes. “He looked at me and we made eye contact. And it’s just like in a movie, the thought that went through my brain was, ‘This man has the bluest eyes I’ve ever seen in my life. I can see all the way to his soul,’ “ she says.Tammy initially thought little more of the encounter than a memorable meeting with a local celebrity. That changed when Bradshaw left her a voicemail she described as the “most unassuming, sweet voicemail.” He had obtained her number through an acquaintance who worked at the hospital.She was nervous about accepting his invitation because of his fame, but the first date went well. “I had such a good time with him and I could tell he was a good person.”A good first date did not settle Tammy’s concerns. Bradshaw kept calling, but she often let the phone ring. The question was whether she felt ready to enter a relationship with someone whose life was so different from hers.“He kept calling and I kept not answering the phone. I was going, ‘Can I do this?’ ... He’s in a whole different world. ‘Am I confident enough to even think about entering this situation?’ “ she says.Her daughter, Lacey Hester, now 37, encouraged her to give the relationship a chance. Tammy and Bradshaw went on to date for more than a decade before marrying in 2014. They renewed their vows in 2021.Their long courtship was not without setbacks. Bradshaw continued to struggle with fears linked to his previous marriages and divorces. At times, he pulled away, once ending the relationship through an email. The separation lasted months.“I would get scared,” he admits. “I didn’t trust myself, honestly.”Tammy said she understood that Bradshaw, who lives with clinical depression, was working to find the right treatment plan, including medication. She chose not to pressure him into making decisions before he was ready.“I learned to stand still and he would always come back,” she says.Looking back, Bradshaw believes those personal struggles ultimately brought them together. “Personal struggles is what got me to her,” he reflects. “If it hadn’t been for this, it couldn’t have been that.”The couple now speak openly about how fortunate they feel to have found each other. Tammy also appreciates that Bradshaw can publicly express his love for her, a gesture she says she rarely gets to return in the same way. Their story began with a chance hospital encounter, but it endured because both were willing to work through the uncertainty that followed.
Article Summary: Terry Bradshaw and Tammy Bradshaw first met in a Texas hospital in 2003. Bradshaw had been through three divorces and was trying to focus on his mental health. The couple went on to date for more than a decade before marrying in 2014. They renewed their vows in 2021.
